thread:
alex: Quick thread - noticed a regression with KV cache during continuous batching merges. Long-context tests show steady RSS growth and ~4k "ghost" KV entries that never get reclaimed.

alex: Perf snapshot attached from last run:
```
kv_cache.total_entries=120720
kv_cache.resident=116345
kv_cache.ghost_refs=4021
kv_cache.frag_bytes=1.2GB
mem.rss=18.2GB
batch.merge_count=8423
batch.split_count=237
continuous.batch_window_ms=14
```

maria: ugh. repro steps? I can run locally.

alex: repro is the long_context_merge scenario in runtime testsuite. Command:
```
./tools/runtime_perf --profile=kv_long_ctx --batches=continuous --ctx_len=8192 --runs=200 --seed=42
```
I can share the small trace (10 GB) - it's noisy but shows merge spikes at ~60k tokens.

jonathan: Curious - do the ghost entries have live refs or are they orphaned? my theory: merge path is duplicating KV slots and dropping one codepath that should decrement refcount on split.

alex: looked at the heapmap - most ghost keys are duplicates of recently-accessed slots with identical key hashes. refcounts for those slots are 0 according to our internal counter, but we still account them in resident set.

rachel: can you run with --kv-debug and dump the slot table around a merge event? also try light ASAN build on host CPU to catch stray frees (I know GPU code can't asan, but the allocator glue might be on host).

alex: did that. snippet from the slot table dump around merge:
```
[slot 12345] state=RESIDENT ref=0 last_gen=58232 alias_of=12340
[slot 12346] state=GHOST ref=0 last_gen=58232 alias_of=12340
[slot 12347] state=RESIDENT ref=1 last_gen=58233
```
So we have alias_of pointing to a parent slot; ghost slots never moved to free state because free_list.append() was skipped in merge split path.

jonathan: sounds like an ordering bug: we flush merged KV to new slot then update alias_of but only call free_list.append() on split done path. If a racing batch tries to reuse the slot meantime, it increments refcount incorrectly.

sam: quick mitigation idea: make merge atomic w.r.t. slot lifecycle. Either a small global spin or flip a slot-state enum to MERGING -> MERGED -> FREE; ensure free_list appended in same atomic transition. We can also throttle merges when kv_frag_ratio > 0.12 to avoid hot path.

maria: +1 for throttling as short-term. Add a metric kv_frag_ratio = kv_cache.frag_bytes / total_cache_bytes and avoid merge if ratio trending up.

alex: did a PoC: added a guard in continuous batching: if kv_frag_ratio > 0.1 skip cross-batch merge for 200ms. RSS growth stopped in 3 runs. Not a fix but promising.

rachel: for long-term we need a unit test that exercises interleaved merge+reuse. Can we write a deterministic harness that simulates two batches racing on same slot? If so we'll catch the ordering bug in CI.

jonathan: I'll prototype a failing test that simulates the split/merge sequence and assert free_list length invariant after merge. Also will add an assert in free_list.append() under debug builds to catch double-skip.

perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: s3://perf/redwood/kv/1767777777/flame.svg (merge spikes at 1m20s) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: filing issue with repro trace + small dump. assigning to @jonathan for fix, @maria to add throttling metric, @rachel to add CI harness. I'll post patch attempts here.

sam: FYI we should also check kernel selection consequences - if an optimized kernel delays KV write-back timing that could widen the race window. low-prio follow-up.

rachel: noted. scheduling short sync tomorrow 10am PT. thanks all :thumbsup:
